topic: Introduction to aero-elasticity, classification, effects of structural distortion, wing torsional divergence, control effective and reversal
syllabus_extract: Introduction to aero-elasticity, classification, effects of structural distortion, wing torsional divergence, control effective and reversal. introduction to flutter, control surface flutter, wing bending torsional flutter, factor effecting flutter characteristics, aileron buzz, buffeting, dynamic response, effect of sweep on various critical speeds
specific_objectives: 11.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain aircraft structure, various structural elements and their details.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of wing torsional divergence diagrams; Instructor supervision required for safety regarding structural load limits.
intro_questions: List three types of structural distortion.
What is the primary cause of wing torsional divergence?

development.content:
Introduction to aero-elasticity concepts
Classification of aero-elastic effects
Effects of structural distortion
Wing torsional divergence mechanism
Control effectiveness and reversal

Introduction to flutter phenomena
Control surface flutter characteristics
Wing bending torsional flutter modes
Factors affecting flutter characteristics
Aileron buzz and buffeting effects

topics: Effect of sweep on critical speeds
development.content:
Dynamic response of airframes
Effect of sweep on critical speeds
Summary of aero-elastic limits
Review of divergence and flutter
Preparation for panel buckling loads

summary_questions: Explain the difference between divergence and flutter.
How does wing sweep affect critical flutter speed?
Identify two factors that influence flutter characteristics.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the relationship between wing sweep and critical speeds for the next lesson on panel buckling estimation.

pft_rows.syllabus: Panel bucking, estimation of compressive loads for bucking a panel on simply supported structures. Rigidity due to end conditions on panel, study of heads, to bend panel with regards to variation in end condition shear buckling of plates
